title: Oklahoma takes out frustration on Ole Miss, knocks Rebels from Playoff race
content:
In the end, Ole Miss only delayed its elimination by one day.

The Rebels, national semifinalists last season and early-season contenders after beating former coach Lane Kiffin and LSU, saw their hopes of returning to the College Football Playoff end on a cold, rainy Sunday afternoon in Oklahoma.

Oklahoma, itself a disappointing team after a CFP bid last year, braved a postponement, the weather and a late Trinidad Chambliss Hail Mary attempt to win 24-17.

Though some Saturday kickoff times were adjusted, Oklahoma-Ole Miss was the only college football game moved back a day after Friday’s FAA ground stop order, much to the Sooners’ consternation. Oklahoma athletic director Roger Denny criticized Ole Miss and the SEC office for not doing enough to make a Saturday game work.

“Everybody was real irritated with the situation,” Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer told ESPN after the game. “But it was still fun.”

No. 19 Ole Miss (6-4, 4-4 SEC) joined the flurry of SEC teams whose Playoff hopes almost certainly ended this weekend: No. 11 Kentucky, No. 17 South Carolina, No. 21 LSU and No. 22 Missouri all lost Saturday. The Rebels had stronger hopes after a 5-1 start, but they have lost three of four — and now have the same record as the Sooners (6-4, 4-3, who have won three of four. That includes two straight since Jason Witten became the interim offensive coordinator after Ben Arbuckle’s firing.

While Ole Miss had its way with the schedule, Oklahoma had its way with Ole Miss — at least for three quarters.

Oklahoma jumped ahead early in the fourth quarter, with Isaiah Sategna’s 75-yard punt return making it 14-0. The Sooners looked like they were about to put it away when Tate Sandell lined up for a 39-yard field goal that would have made it 24-7.

But the normally reliable Sandell missed wide right, and Chambliss responded with a touchdown drive, following a 32-yard scramble on third-and-15 with a 26-yard touchdown strike to Caleb Odom.

Sandell got another chance from almost the same spot with 4:58 left, and this time he nailed it to give the Sooners a 10-point lead.

The Rebels did draw back within seven with 42 seconds left on a Lucas Carneiro field goal. Without any timeouts, they had to try an onside kick, and they recovered.

They couldn’t get closer than the 29, where Chambliss had one final play with 7 seconds left. He rolled right and heaved to the end zone, where Odom, in a muddle of bodies, couldn’t haul it in as the ball bounced off his helmet.
